reviews.reason: Four pieces, equal material and one checking move convert the visible alignment into a safe rook capture. The played game reaches the same payoff.
reviews.distinctness: The first new Skewer position teaches a horizontal king skewer by a rook. The black king covers the capture square, including when the white king stays adjacent after Ke4 or Kf2.
reviews.solutionVi: Ra3+ — Xe đen từ a4 đến a3, chiếu Vua trắng trên hàng 3. Vua trắng phải rời hàng này. Xe đen có thể bắt Xe trắng ở f3. Vua đen ở g4 bảo vệ ô f3 nên Vua trắng không thể bắt lại.
hintsVi: Quan sát vị trí của Vua trắng và Xe trắng trên cùng một hàng.
Tìm nước chiếu bằng Xe đen trên hàng 3.
Đưa Xe đen từ a4 đến a3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The e3 king blocks the third rank to the rook on f3. The check from a3 clears that line with tempo. Black cannot take f3 with the king at the start because White’s king protects the rook.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 15 legal Black moves have resolved short-horizon outcomes. Re4+ loses the rook to Kxe4; Rf4 allows Rxf4+. The quiet alternatives do not force a gain, and the engine comparison finds no competing winning or mating line.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ke4, Kd4, Kf2, Ke2 and Kd2 are the five legal replies. The white rook cannot reach a blocking square through its own king or capture the attacker. Rxf3 (with check after Kf2) keeps a full rook through all 20 immediate replies; the black king protects f3. After Kd2, Kxf3 is also available as a follow-up to the same skewer.
reviewNotes.level: The learner makes only Ra3+. There are four pieces, no sacrifice and no preparatory move. The capture is the explanation of the gain and is outside the playable line.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete 154-ply game, Nguyễn Ngọc Trường Sơn–Parham Maghsoodloo, 2026-09-03, TWIC 1661. The original position follows 76.Ke3. The game continuation is 76...Ra3+ 77.Ke4 Rxf3, with the archived source URL and SHA-256 attached.

reviews.reason: Equal four-piece position. Only the file check creates a material gain, and the nearby white king reduces the defence to one visible retreat.
reviews.distinctness: The white king cuts off g4 and g5 to force Kg3. Its job is to control escape squares, unlike the preserved rook example where the solving king guards the rear capture square.
reviews.solutionVi: Rh1+ — Xe trắng từ g1 đến h1, chiếu Vua đen dọc cột h. Vua trắng khống chế g4 và g5 nên Vua đen chỉ còn ô g3. Xe trắng sau đó bắt Xe đen ở h6.
hintsVi: Vua đen và Xe đen đang đứng trên cùng một cột.
Tìm nước chiếu bằng Xe trắng trên cột h.
Đưa Xe trắng từ g1 đến h1. Vua trắng đang khống chế g4 và g5.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: From h1 the rook checks the king on h4 and, once that king leaves the file, attacks the rook on h6. There is no comparable direct capture.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 17 legal roots and their engine lines replay. Rg4+ Kh3 fails to align the rook with h6. Rg6 Rxg6 Kxg6 only exchanges rooks. Other starts fail the short material objective and no alternative has a positive mate score.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kg3 is the only reply: Rh1 controls the h-file while Kf5 cuts off g4 and g5. Rxh6 retains the full rook through Kf3, Kg4 and Kg2. No check evasion can capture the attacker or interpose.
reviewNotes.level: Four pieces, equal material and a single quiet check. The follow-up capture explains the result and is outside the one-move exercise.
reviewNotes.provenance: Hartge–Clawitter, 17 March 2026, TWIC 1637. The complete 177-ply game replays to the exact FEN after 71...Rh6, then 72.Rh1+ Kg3 73.Rxh6. The archive link, checksum and master title are recorded.

reviews.reason: Equal four-piece position with a unique check that wins the exposed queen in one visible follow-up.
reviews.distinctness: An apparently natural short-range queen check is unsafe. The long diagonal move from c6 to g2 turns into a check along the g-file while White’s king blocks its own queen’s access to the checking piece.
reviews.solutionVi: Qg2+ — Hậu đen từ c6 đến g2, chiếu Vua trắng trên cột g. Khi Vua trắng rời cột g, Hậu đen bắt Hậu trắng ở g8.
hintsVi: Vua và Hậu trắng đang đứng trên cùng một cột.
Tìm ô trên cột g để Hậu đen chiếu từ xa, ngoài tầm bắt của Vua trắng.
Đưa Hậu đen từ c6 đến g2.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The king on g5 lies between the checking square g2 and queen g8. White’s own king stops the rear queen from taking or interposing along that file. Only the checking alignment gives Black the queen.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 28 roots have resolved short-horizon outcomes, and no competing root shows a mating score. Qc5+ allows Kf6 without winning a piece, and Qh6+ allows Kxh6. The best non-skewer engine alternatives score approximately equal.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The six replies are Kh6, Kf6, Kh5, Kf5, Kh4 and Kf4. Each allows Qxg8, and all 17 legal replies after that capture retain the queen gain. No reply can capture or interpose against the initial checking queen.
reviewNotes.level: Equal material, four pieces, a single quiet checking move and one clear follow-up. No capture or sacrifice is needed to create the skewer.
reviewNotes.provenance: Southcott-Moyers–Arakelyan, Titled Tue 23 December 2025. Full legal game replay reaches the exact FEN at ply 135 after Kg5, followed in the game by Qg2+ Kf6 Qxg8. The TWIC 1625 archive URL and SHA-256 are attached.

reviews.reason: Four pieces, one forcing rook check, and an immediate visible bishop win. The extra exchange value at the start is meaningful only once the bishop is taken.
reviews.distinctness: The only king escape is set by the opposing king’s control of b4 and b5. The learner must make the check from the a-file, rather than from b5, and can see the entire four-piece line without calculating a recapture.
reviews.solutionVi: Ra8+ — Xe trắng từ b8 đến a8, chiếu Vua đen trên cột a. Vua đen chỉ có thể đi đến b6. Sau đó, Xe trắng bắt được Tượng ở a3.
hintsVi: Quan sát cột a. Quân nào đứng phía sau Vua đen?
Tìm nước chiếu bằng Xe trên cùng cột với Vua đen và Tượng đen.
Đưa Xe trắng từ b8 đến a8.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Ra8+ attacks the king at a5 from above the bishop at a3. The king stands between the rook and bishop and leaves the line on Kb6.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 19 legal roots replayed and the bounded two-solver-move material test has only Ra8+. Rb5+ allows Ka6 with no bishop win. Rb4 can lose the rook to Bxb4. The next engine root is only +47 cp, and there is no immediate or forced mate in two at the start.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kb6 is the only legal defence. Rxa3 is legal, and the three subsequent legal king moves all leave White a full bishop gained. No piece is offered by Ra8+.
reviewNotes.level: Four pieces and one visible file check. The learner plays Ra8+ and the capture belongs to the explanation.
reviewNotes.provenance: Topencik–Brozzi, Titled Tuesday, 4 August 2026, TWIC 1657. Replayed all 191 plies from the initial game FEN, checked the game ID and source SHA-256 reference, and matched the start after 83...Ka5. The game played 84.Ra8+ Kb6 85.Rxa3.

reviews.reason: A diagonal check wins the rook from a slight material deficit. The other bishop check gives up the bishop immediately.
reviews.distinctness: Choose between two bishop checks. The nearer check at c5 loses to the king, while the longer diagonal from g7 reaches the rook without needing support at a1.
reviews.solutionVi: Bg7+ — Tượng đen từ f8 đến g7, chiếu Vua trắng trên đường chéo g7–a1. Khi Vua rời đường chéo, Tượng bắt Xe ở a1. Nếu chiếu ở c5, Vua trắng có thể bắt Tượng.
hintsVi: Tìm đường chéo đi qua Vua trắng và Xe ở a1.
Xem nước chiếu nào vừa an toàn cho Tượng, vừa nhắm tới Xe.
Đưa Tượng đen từ f8 đến g7.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The g7–a1 diagonal passes through the king on d4. Only the check on that line creates the immediate attack on the rook behind it.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 13 legal roots were compared. Bc5+ allows Kxc5. The strongest quiet try f5 allows Ra8 and supplies no forcing gain. No competing mate was found.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Six legal king retreats allow Bxa1. All 57 immediate recovery replies leave the full rook gain. The check and the capture need no offer or recapture.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces, with the pawns away from the attack line. The task is the single move Bg7+, with one plain contrast to Bc5+.
reviewNotes.provenance: The complete 136-ply game is preserved from TWIC 1646, with the recorded 50...Bg7+ after Rxa1. The played continuation Ke4 Bxa1 reaches the same payoff.

reviews.reason: White is a pawn down with two rooks on each side. The g-rook can check safely and win a full rook. The obvious capture Rxa6 does not secure even a pawn within the same horizon because Black can insert Rh4+.
reviews.distinctness: The learner must choose between two white rooks and rule out a pawn capture by checking for an intervening check. This differs from a single-rook skewer or a case in which the king merely guards the rear capture square.
reviews.solutionVi: Rg3+ — Xe trắng từ g6 đến g3, chiếu Vua đen trên hàng 3. Khi Vua đen rời hàng này, Xe trắng bắt Xe đen ở a3. Xe trắng ở d6 không nên chiếu từ d3 vì Đen có thể bắt Xe đó.
hintsVi: Vua đen ở e3 và Xe đen ở a3 cùng đứng trên hàng 3.
Cả hai Xe trắng đều có thể chiếu. Hãy tìm ô chiếu mà Vua đen không thể bắt Xe.
Đưa Xe trắng từ g6 đến g3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The rook on g3 checks Ke3 from the far side of the rank, so each king retreat exposes Ra3. The g3 checking square lies outside the black king’s reach.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 26 legal roots were checked, including a separate full four-ply comparison allowing ordinary exchanges. Rxa6 Rxa6 Rxa6 can gain a pawn, but Black can instead play Rh4+; Kg1 and Kg3 both allow ...Rxa6 before White can secure the gain. Rd3+ also fails to Kxd3 or Rxd3. The main skewer is the only settled gain within two learner moves.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kf4, Kf2 and Ke2 are the only legal replies. Rxa3 retains a full rook through all 53 immediate replies after those captures, including the Rh4+ countercheck after Kf2 or Ke2.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces. White must choose the safe rook check from two possible rook checks. No preparation or sacrifice is needed. Rxa3 explains the payoff outside the one-move exercise.
reviewNotes.provenance: Shuvalova–Aalto, 26 March 2026, TWIC 1638. Exact position after 53...Ke3 in the complete 131-ply game. The game continues 54.Rg3+ Kf2 55.Rxa3. Archive checksum and master titles are retained.

reviews.reason: The balanced position contrasts a safe diagonal check with several checks that lose the attacking queen outright.
reviews.distinctness: The queen moves just one square along a rank to find the correct diagonal. Grabbing the pawn with check is a concrete trap because White’s king captures the queen.
reviews.solutionVi: Qh3+ — Hậu đen từ g3 đến h3, chiếu Vua trắng theo đường chéo h3–d7. Khi Vua trắng rời đường chéo, Hậu đen bắt Hậu trắng ở d7.
hintsVi: Vua f5 và Hậu d7 của Trắng nằm trên cùng một đường chéo.
Đừng vội bắt Tốt f4. Hãy tìm một nước chiếu mà Vua trắng không thể bắt Hậu đen.
Đưa Hậu đen từ g3 đến h3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: From h3 the queen attacks f5 with d7 behind it. None of Black’s other checks lines up both pieces safely, and the queen on d7 is otherwise out of reach.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 22 legal roots were resolved. The natural Qxf4+ allows Kxf4, and Qd3+ allows Qxd3. Qg4+, Qg5+ and Qg6+ also lose the checking queen to the king. The best alternative a5 scores -47 cp in the bounded comparison.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kg6, Kf6, Kg5, Ke5 and Ke4 all allow Qxd7. All 22 immediate replies after the capture retain the full queen gain. The five independent engine defence searches preserve Black’s advantage.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces and equal material. The contrast between the adjacent pawn capture and the safe check is visible at once, and the learner plays only the quiet check.
reviewNotes.provenance: Galaktionov–Ambartsumova, Titled Tue 2 June 2026, from TWIC 1648 with archive checksum. The original frame follows Kf5 at ply 125. The game actually continued Qh3+ Ke5 Qxd7.

reviews.reason: The immediate king capture loses the exposed rook. The skewer changes the order, saving the rook with check and letting it take a knight on a square protected by the white king.
reviews.distinctness: Unlike a bare rook-versus-rook skewer, the tempting shortcut is a legal capture by White’s king on c5. The learner keeps the rook safe and reuses the king as support for the rook capture. The other rook check can lose to the knight.
reviews.solutionVi: Rf5+ — Xe trắng từ f4 đến f5, chiếu Vua đen trên hàng 5. Khi Vua đen rời hàng, Xe trắng bắt được Mã ở c5. Vua trắng ở b6 bảo vệ ô c5.
hintsVi: Vua đen và Mã đen đang đứng trên cùng một hàng.
Nếu Vua trắng bắt Mã ngay, Đen có thể bắt Xe ở đâu?
Đưa Xe trắng từ f4 đến f5 để chiếu trước.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rf5+ moves the rook away from the black king’s immediate attack and lines it up with Ke5 and Nc5. The king must move before the rook can reach c5.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 25 legal roots replayed. Kxc5 Kxf4 loses a rook for a knight. Re4+ Nxe4 gives up the rook. Rc4 or Rh4 does not force a gain and permits Nxa4+ and other defences. The +237 cp bounded runner-up does not reach the short material objective, while the skewer is +548 cp. No starting mate in one or two.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ke6, Kd6, Ke4, and Kd4 all permit Rxc5, with check after Ke6. All 52 recovery replies keep the full knight gain. Bh3 protects the checking square f5, and Kb6 controls c5.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces. The wrong capture and wrong check each fail to a single visible reply. The one learner move is a direct check with no sacrifice or preparation.
reviewNotes.provenance: Mikhailovsky–Soto, Titled Tuesday, 13 October 2026, TWIC 1667. Replayed the full 137 plies and matched the exact start after 57...Rxe7, the preceding FEN, played SAN, game hash and archive reference. The game played 58.Rf5+ Kd4 59.Rxc5.

reviews.reason: The bishop chooses the diagonal that skewers the rook. Black’s king stops White’s king from recapturing on the far square.
reviews.distinctness: A supported bishop skewer with two real diagonal checks to compare. The opponent’s king can step adjacent to the rear rook, so support on d7 matters.
reviews.solutionVi: Bf5+ — Tượng đen từ b1 đến f5, chiếu Vua trắng trên đường chéo f5–d7. Khi Vua rời đường chéo, Tượng bắt Xe ở d7. Vua đen ở e8 bảo vệ ô d7 nên Vua trắng không thể bắt lại Tượng.
hintsVi: Tìm đường chéo nối Vua trắng với Xe ở d7.
So sánh hai nước chiếu bằng Tượng. Kiểm tra quân nào bảo vệ ô d7.
Đưa Tượng đen từ b1 đến f5.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bf5+ attacks Ke6 with Rd7 directly behind. The king on e8 already covers d7 and neutralizes the rear king recapture only once the diagonal is cleared.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 10 legal moves were compared. Ba2+ Kd6 makes the king move but leaves the rook outside the attack line. Neither pushing a pawn nor another move forces the short gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Four legal king retreats all permit Bxd7. After Kd6, Kxd7 is illegal because Black’s king covers d7. After Kf6, White can take the g6 pawn, leaving at least four pawns of net material gain over the start. All 21 immediate replies were checked.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces. The visible decision is which diagonal to check on and whether d7 is protected. The passed pawn needs no calculation for the material task.
reviewNotes.provenance: The 112-ply TWIC 1650 game follows Kxe6 with 50...Bf5+ Kf6 51...Bxd7 in the actual game. The indexed headers, archive checksum and preceding frame match.

reviews.reason: Balanced queen ending with several superficially attractive checks. A long check along the g-file is the only way to force the immediate queen gain.
reviews.distinctness: The choice is between a safe long-range check and close checks that let the king take the queen. Qe8+ even allows a king retreat that still protects h5. Both queens have just promoted in the source, but the learner solves the line attack without needing the preceding race.
reviews.solutionVi: Qg8+ — Hậu trắng từ h8 đến g8, chiếu Vua đen dọc cột g. Khi Vua đen rời cột này, Hậu trắng bắt Hậu đen ở g1. Nếu chiếu từ h7, Hậu trắng sẽ đứng sát Vua đen và có thể bị bắt.
hintsVi: Vua đen và Hậu đen cùng đứng trên cột g.
Tìm nước chiếu từ xa để Vua đen không thể bắt Hậu trắng.
Đưa Hậu trắng từ h8 đến g8.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qg8+ establishes the line g8–g6–g1. The black king shields its queen from the line until it retreats, and its own queen cannot interpose through the king.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 24 roots were checked. Qh7+, Qh6+, Qg7+, Qf6+ and Qxh5+ allow the king to take the queen. Qe8+ Kh6 protects h5 and stops the short pawn gain. No alternative root showed a positive mate score or a comparable short gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kh6, Kf6 and Kf5 all allow Qxg1. All nine immediate replies after these captures leave White a full queen up from the starting balance. The checked side has no legal block or capture of the attacker.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces, equal material and direct choice of the safe checking square. The first move is the only move played in the exercise.
reviewNotes.provenance: Tanenbaum–Ivanytska, 13 November 2025, TWIC 1620. The complete 137-ply game gives the exact position after 57...Kg6 and the played continuation 58.Qg8+ Kf5 59.Qxg1. The archived game, checksum and titles are recorded.

reviews.reason: Two rooks convert an equal immediate exchange into a protected rook capture. The second rook’s role explains why the check matters.
reviews.distinctness: The rear rook can already be captured directly at the start, but only for an even trade. Creating the skewer first activates mutual protection along the file, including after the white king retreats beside b3.
reviews.solutionVi: Rb6+ — Xe đen từ a6 đến b6, chiếu Vua trắng trên cột b. Sau khi Vua trắng rời cột, Xe từ b6 có thể bắt Xe trắng ở b3. Xe đen ở b1 bảo vệ ô b3, nên Vua trắng không thể bắt lại.
hintsVi: Xe đen ở b1 có thể bắt Xe b3 ngay, nhưng Vua trắng có thể bắt lại.
Hãy dùng Xe a6 để chiếu trước và phối hợp hai Xe trên cột b.
Đưa Xe đen từ a6 đến b6.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The rook on b6 checks the king through b5 while the enemy rook on b3 is behind it. The rook on b1 both attacks b3 and protects the checking rook’s capture there.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 25 legal roots were compared. Rxb3+ Kxb3 is an even trade and Ra4+ Kxa4 drops the attacker. The bounded runner-up Rc1 at +206 cp does not force a short material gain. The skewer is the only positive result at the shared material horizon.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The six king replies Kc5, Ka5, Kc4, Ka4, Kc3 and Ka3 all allow R6xb3 or R6xb3+. None captures the checking rook. Of 53 replies after this witness, Rxe6 can recover a pawn in four branches, leaving a net gain worth four pawns. The published explanation uses the valid R6xb3 follow-up without calling it the move played in the game.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces and a one-pawn initial difference. The main choice is to check before taking. Both the tempting even exchange and the second rook’s support are visible from the start.
reviewNotes.provenance: Dreelinck–Kononenko, 26 March 2026, checksummed TWIC 1638 archive. The position follows Kb4 at ply 85. The game played Rb6+ Kc5 R1xb3, using the other rook to take after the same skewer.

reviews.reason: The black queen remains active and can take the white bishop or deliver checks. The only short material win is to choose the far end of the queen’s diagonal, avoiding tempting checks that immediately lose the queen.
reviews.distinctness: White changes diagonals with Qa2–b1, exploiting the opposing queen as both the rear target and the refutation to Qd5+. This differs from the rank-to-diagonal Qh3+ example and from a skewer in which the rear piece can only escape after a king move.
reviews.solutionVi: Qb1+ — Hậu trắng từ a2 đến b1, chiếu Vua đen ở d3 theo đường chéo. Khi Vua đen rời đường chéo b1–f5, Hậu trắng có thể bắt Hậu đen ở f5.
hintsVi: Xác định đường chéo đi qua Vua đen ở d3 và Hậu đen ở f5.
Tìm nước chiếu từ phía bên kia Vua. Nếu chiếu từ d5, Hậu đen có thể bắt Hậu trắng không?
Đưa Hậu trắng từ a2 đến b1.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The queen check from b1 puts Qb1, Kd3 and Qf5 on one diagonal. White cannot take f5 from a2. Checking from b1 simultaneously gets the queen onto the line and removes the king with tempo.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 35 legal roots replayed, no starting mate in one or two, and only Qb1+ meets the bounded material goal. Qd5+ Qxd5 loses the queen; Qa6+ Kd2 escapes the attack without exposing the queen. The next engine root Qg8 is +88 cp and allows active queen checks.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kc4, Ke3, Ke2, and Kd2 are all the legal replies. Qxf5 is legal after each, and all 17 subsequent legal replies retain the full queen gain. The defender cannot interpose or capture the attacker.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces. One quiet queen move gives check, and the rear queen is immediately visible. No additional learner move or sacrifice is required.
reviewNotes.provenance: Chirilov–Gunebakan, 27 August 2026, TWIC 1660. Replayed all 129 plies and matched the exact start after 58...Qf5, preceding FEN, game hash and archive SHA-256 reference. 59.Qb1+ Ke3 60.Qxf5 was played.

reviews.reason: The learner must distinguish a sound check from a check that gives up the rook and from a pawn capture that is immediately recaptured.
reviews.distinctness: Three contrasting actions by the same rook. The defending king may counter by taking a pawn elsewhere, yet the skewer still wins substantial material.
reviews.solutionVi: Rh3+ — Xe đen từ h4 đến h3, chiếu Vua trắng trên hàng 3. Khi Vua rời hàng, Xe đen bắt Xe ở c3. Nếu Vua trắng bắt Tốt f5 sau đó, Đen vẫn có lợi vì bắt được Xe và chỉ mất một Tốt.
hintsVi: Vua trắng và Xe trắng đang đứng trên cùng hàng nào?
So sánh hai nước chiếu bằng Xe. Ở ô nào Xe đen có thể bị Vua trắng bắt?
Đưa Xe đen từ h4 đến h3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The third-rank check forces Kf3 off the line to Rc3. From h4 there is neither a legal direct capture of Rc3 nor a protected check on f4.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 17 legal roots were compared. Rf4+ Kxf4 loses the rook. Rxc4 Rxc4 exchanges a rook for a pawn. Rg4 lets White move or advance the c-pawn without losing Rc3.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All four king replies allow Rxc3. White can reply Kxf5 after Kf4, reducing the gain from a full rook to rook for pawn. None of the 22 immediate recovery replies can take the attacking rook.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces and one checking move. The learner can see both traps with ordinary rook and king moves.
reviewNotes.provenance: The complete 132-ply game from TWIC 1652 records Rc3, 57...Rh3+ Kf4 58...Rxc3 Kxf5. The saved preceding frame and checked archive identify the original position.

reviews.reason: White is down material and must exploit the black king’s alignment now. The white king guards f6, and even Black’s capture of a pawn after the skewer leaves a clear net gain.
reviews.distinctness: Unlike the preserved four-piece example, the learner is recovering from a material deficit and must account for a separate knight capture on h3. A rival rook check sends the king away without winning the rook.
reviews.solutionVi: Rf3+ — Xe trắng từ c3 đến f3, chiếu Vua đen dọc cột f. Khi Vua đen rời cột này, Xe trắng bắt Xe đen ở f6. Vua trắng ở e7 bảo vệ f6. Ngay cả khi Mã đen bắt Tốt h3, Trắng vẫn giữ được lợi thế vật chất.
hintsVi: Quan sát Vua đen ở f5 và Xe đen ở f6.
Tìm nước chiếu trên cột f. Vua trắng đang bảo vệ ô f6.
Đưa Xe trắng từ c3 đến f3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The rook must check along the same file as Kf5 and Rf6. White’s king guards f6 against a king recapture and makes the gain safe after the retreat.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 18 roots were checked. Rc5+ Kg6 leaves the black rook outside the white rook’s attack. Quiet Re3 allows ...Rb6 and loses the alignment. White starts down a knight for a pawn, and no other starting move secures the short gain or shows a positive mating score.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kg6, Kg5, Ke5 and Ke4 all allow Rxf6, with check after Kg6. All 36 immediate replies after the captures preserve a rook gain or a rook for a pawn if ...Nxh3 is available. No king can capture on protected f6.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces. The deciding move is an immediate rook check and the capture is visible. Counting the separate pawn loss does not require a longer solution.
reviewNotes.provenance: Javakhadze–Nguyen Thi Phuong Anh, 18 August 2026, TWIC 1659. The complete 169-ply game reaches the exact position after 54...Kf5. The source continues 55.Rf3+ Ke5 56.Rxf6. Archive checksum and master credentials are retained.

reviews.reason: Black starts behind and must pick the one check that attacks along the first rank. The forced king exit is easy to trace.
reviews.distinctness: A lone king exit after a back-rank queen check contrasts with a tempting check from h3 that leads to the same king move but leaves no attack on a1. The learner follows the line through the king instead of merely finding any check.
reviews.solutionVi: Qh1+ — Hậu đen từ h4 đến h1, chiếu Vua trắng trên hàng 1. Vua trắng chỉ có thể đi từ f1 đến e2. Hậu đen sau đó bắt Hậu trắng ở a1.
hintsVi: Vua f1 và Hậu a1 của Trắng đứng trên cùng một hàng.
Tìm ô trên hàng 1 để Hậu đen chiếu Vua và cùng lúc nhắm về a1.
Đưa Hậu đen từ h4 đến h1.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: From h1 the queen checks the king f1 with queen a1 on the same ray behind it. The king cannot stay on that rank, and its own body blocks the rear queen from intervening along the ray.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 17 legal moves were compared. Qh3+ Ke2 leaves a1 unattacked, Qxf2+ loses the queen to Kxf2, and Qxc4+ loses it to Bxc4. All alternative roots scored below zero in the bounded review.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ke2 is the only legal reply to Qh1+. Qxa1 is legal, and none of the 11 replies after Qxa1 recovers any material. No sacrifice, interposition or checking counterattack is required in the lesson.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces, but only three pieces matter to the direct decision. Black starts behind by the equivalent of about two pawns, so the tactic creates the material swing.
reviewNotes.provenance: Florescu–To, 26 February 2026, checksummed TWIC 1634 archive. The exact frame follows Qa1 at ply 129. Qh1+ Ke2 Qxa1 is the actual game sequence.

reviews.reason: The learner chooses between several checks, including a rook check that gives away the rook, and selects the safe rank check that exposes the bishop in every branch.
reviews.distinctness: The refuting king capture Kxf6 is an immediate, visible error check. White could also give a knight check, but that does not force the gain. After the game’s particular defence a separate mate was available, while the same rear-piece capture works across all four replies.
reviews.solutionVi: Rh5+ — Xe trắng từ h6 đến h5, chiếu Vua đen trên hàng 5. Khi Vua đen rời hàng, Xe trắng có thể bắt Tượng ở c5. Nếu đưa Xe đến f6 để chiếu, Vua đen có thể bắt Xe.
hintsVi: Tìm hàng có cả Vua đen và Tượng đen.
So sánh hai nước chiếu bằng Xe. Sau nước nào Vua đen có thể bắt Xe?
Đưa Xe trắng từ h6 đến h5.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rh5+ reaches the same rank as Kf5 and Bc5 and requires the king to leave it. The rook begins on h6 and cannot take c5 directly.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 25 legal roots replayed and there is no starting mate in one or two. Rf6+ can be met by Kxf6. Nh4+ can be met by Ke5 and does not force short gain. White has an initial 190 cp material edge, but the alternatives, including the +288 cp engine runner-up, do not obtain the bishop or guarantee comparable immediate material.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kg6, Kf6, Ke6, and Kg4 all permit the illustrative Rxc5. All 66 subsequent legal replies preserve the bishop gain. The rook on h5 cannot be captured or the check blocked. After Kg4 only, the actual game used the legal immediate Rg5# instead of the illustrative capture.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces. The immediate difference between safe Rh5+ and unsafe Rf6+ is visible without calculating the later game mate.
reviewNotes.provenance: Martinez Alcantara–Dinesh, 7 October 2025, TWIC 1614. Replayed all 111 plies, matched the start after 54...Kf5 and verified the preceding FEN, game hash and source reference. 55.Rh5+ is played; Rxc5 is the verified analysis continuation. The actual final moves were 55...Kg4 56.Rg5#.

reviews.reason: A quiet bishop check forces an exchange gain, even when the opposing king remains close enough to take the bishop after it captures.
reviews.distinctness: The bishop cannot rely on a protected rear square. The learner must recognize that a legal king recapture still leaves a rook-for-bishop gain.
reviews.solutionVi: Bd4+ — Tượng đen từ g7 đến d4, chiếu Vua trắng trên đường chéo d4–g1. Khi Vua rời đường chéo, Tượng bắt Xe ở g1. Nếu Vua trắng bắt lại Tượng, Đen vẫn có lợi vì đã đổi Tượng lấy Xe.
hintsVi: Tìm đường chéo đi qua Vua trắng và Xe ở g1.
Nếu Vua trắng bắt lại quân ở g1, Đen đổi quân nào lấy quân nào?
Đưa Tượng đen từ g7 đến d4.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: From d4 the bishop attacks Kf2 and the rook on g1 is behind it. The initial bishop cannot capture the rook or a loose piece to obtain the same gain.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 18 roots were compared. A retreat such as Bf8 allows Rf1, taking the rook out of the combination. The engine favours Black somewhat in the pawn structure, but other moves do not force the immediate exchange gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All six legal retreats permit Bxg1. After Kg2 or Kf1, Kxg1 takes the bishop, leaving at least +170 cp in material relative to the start. Other replies retain a full rook gain. All 32 immediate replies were checked. The root gives nothing away.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces, with the pawns well away from the diagonal. The only task is to choose Bd4+ and recognize the value of the next exchange.
reviewNotes.provenance: TWIC 1624 contains the complete 176-ply game. After Kxf2, the actual 41...Bd4+ Kf1 42...Bxg1 Kxg1 demonstrates the strongest immediate recovery.

reviews.reason: White is a pawn down after both promotions. The opposing pawns block two king escapes, leaving a single reply to the queen skewer along the a-file.
reviews.distinctness: The opponent’s own pawns on b6 and b7 restrict the king. The other a-file check puts the attacker on the wrong side of the king and allows the rear queen to take it.
reviews.solutionVi: Qa8+ — Hậu trắng từ g8 đến a8, chiếu Vua đen dọc cột a. Hai Tốt đen ở b6 và b7 chặn hai ô thoát, nên Vua đen chỉ còn ô b5. Khi Vua rời cột a, Hậu trắng bắt Hậu đen ở a1.
hintsVi: Vua đen ở a6 và Hậu đen ở a1 cùng đứng trên cột a.
Tìm ô chiếu trên cột a mà Hậu đen không thể bắt.
Đưa Hậu trắng từ g8 đến a8. Hai Tốt đen cản đường Vua ở b6 và b7.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qa8+ checks from beyond the king so the queen at a1 is screened by Ka6. Only after the king moves can the queens attack each other.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 21 roots were checked. Qa2+ allows Qxa2 at once, and Qc4+ b5 lets a pawn block without exposing the queen. Quiet queen moves and g6 do not force immediate material gain. No alternative positive mate score appeared.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kb5 is the only legal reply: a5 and a7 remain on the checking file and Black’s own pawns occupy b6 and b7. Qxa1 survives all four immediate replies, gaining the full queen.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces and one queen move. The previous promotion explains the original game position, but no promotion calculation is required for the solution.
reviewNotes.provenance: Boutikos–Atwell, 10 September 2026, TWIC 1662. Exact source position follows 49...a1=Q. The complete 137-ply game continues 50.Qa8+ Kb5 51.Qxa1. Black’s IM title and the archive checksum are recorded.

reviews.reason: The direct skewer also closes the opposing queen’s countercheck line. Ordinary checks squander Black’s extra knight advantage.
reviews.distinctness: White’s king can vacate the diagonal and reveal a check on b2 after a tempting queen check. The winning square d4 neutralizes that defensive resource while creating the skewer.
reviews.solutionVi: Qd4+ — Hậu đen từ g1 đến d4, chiếu Vua trắng trên đường chéo d4–h8. Hậu đen ở d4 cũng chắn đường chiếu từ h8 đến Vua đen ở b2. Khi Vua trắng rời đường chéo, Hậu đen bắt Hậu trắng ở h8.
hintsVi: Vua e5 đang che đường chéo từ Hậu trắng ở h8 đến Vua đen ở b2.
Tìm ô trên đường chéo đó để Hậu đen vừa chiếu Vua trắng, vừa chắn đường chiếu về b2.
Đưa Hậu đen từ g1 đến d4.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The queen on d4 checks through e5 with the white queen h8 behind it. When the king moves, Black’s queen both prevents a revealed check along h8–b2 and can legally capture h8.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 34 legal moves were resolved. Qg5+ Kd6+ and Qc5+ Ke6+ allow discovered counterchecks. The direct Qg7+ allows Qxg7. Black has an extra knight but the best alternative is only +27 cp in the bounded full-root comparison.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: White can play Ke6 or Kf5. Qxh8 follows in each case. All 11 legal replies after the capture retain the queen gain. The possibility of a revealed check is real after other roots, while d4 keeps the checking line blocked.
reviewNotes.level: Five pieces and a one-move skewer. A beginner can trace the one shared diagonal. The knight is neither sacrificed nor needed for the immediate payoff.
reviewNotes.provenance: Movahed–Le Tuan Minh, 15 October 2026, TWIC 1667 with archive checksum. The source reaches the exact frame after Qh8 at ply 143 and played Qd4+ Kf5 Qxh8.

reviews.reason: The pawn push competes for attention, but the skewer first removes the bishop. The opponent’s rook still has pawn captures, making this a concrete check that the tactical gain survives counterplay.
reviews.distinctness: Unlike the clear bishop win in the four-piece Topencik position, the learner must prefer the forcing file check over pushing a pawn and see why a pawn capture by the opposing rook still leaves a net minor-piece gain.
reviews.solutionVi: Rg8+ — Xe trắng từ a8 đến g8, chiếu Vua đen trên cột g. Khi Vua đen rời cột, Xe trắng bắt được Tượng ở g3. Nếu Xe đen bắt một Tốt ở a6 hoặc g2, Trắng vẫn có lợi về vật chất nhờ đã bắt Tượng.
hintsVi: Vua đen và Tượng đen nằm trên cùng cột nào?
Thử tìm nước chiếu bằng Xe trước khi đẩy Tốt a6.
Đưa Xe trắng từ a8 đến g8.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Moving the rook from a8 to g8 checks Kg6 and exposes Bg3. Starting with a7 gives the black bishop and rook time for counterplay.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 15 legal roots replayed, no starting mate in one or two, and the only bounded short gain is Rg8+. After a7, ...Bf2+ is a practical refutation of a quick gain and the rook can subsequently take on a7 in the shown line. Moving the knight with Nd3 or Nf3 allows ...Ra1+ Ne1 ...Rxe1#, a threat to White rather than a competing win. The next engine root is +21 cp.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kh7, Kf7, Kf6, Kh5, and Kf5 all allow Rxg3. In the 76 recovery replies, the strongest immediate captures ...Rxa6 and ...Rxg2+ can remove only one pawn, leaving at least 230 cp net material gain. The checking rook is neither offered nor recaptured.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces including both kings. The single move creates a visible file skewer. The most important counterplay is one rook capture of a pawn, with the bishop gain easily counted.
reviewNotes.provenance: Gutman–Myagmarsuren, 21 October 2025, TWIC 1616. Replayed all 138 plies and matched the exact start after 50...Bg3, the preceding FEN, played SAN, game ID and archived source reference. 51.Rg8+ Kh7 52.Rxg3 Rxa6 was played. White later lost the game, so the note claims only the short material gain.

reviews.reason: Equal starting material and three plausible checks make the right rook move meaningful. Even a king recapture leaves a clean queen-for-rook gain.
reviews.distinctness: Compare a rook check from the neighboring h-file, a knight check and a tempting pawn capture. The safe file check wins the queen even if the king stays close enough to trade.
reviews.solutionVi: Rg4+ — Xe đen từ h4 đến g4, chiếu Vua trắng trên cột g. Khi Vua rời cột, Xe đen bắt Hậu ở g8. Nếu Vua trắng bắt lại Xe, Đen vẫn có lợi vì đã đổi Xe lấy Hậu.
hintsVi: Tìm cột có cả Vua trắng và Hậu trắng.
Kiểm tra nước chiếu ở h6. Vua trắng có thể bắt Xe ở đó không?
Đưa Xe đen từ h4 đến g4.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The g-file alignment puts Kg6 in front of Qg8. Rg4+ creates the attack on the queen through the king. Taking the a4 pawn immediately leaves the knight exposed.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 27 roots were compared. Rh6+ permits Kxh6, and Rxa4 or Kxa4 permits Qxe6. Nf8+ permits Qxf8. The other quiet moves allow the queen to escape and do not secure the short gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All six king replies allow Rxg8. After Kh7 or Kf7, Kxg8 makes an immediate queen-for-rook exchange. After some other retreats the king can take the e6 knight instead. Each of 19 replies after Rxg8 leaves a material gain of at least four pawns relative to the start.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces, one move, no sacrifice. The learner compares the two rook checks and counts an immediate exchange if needed.
reviewNotes.provenance: The full 126-ply TWIC 1634 game records Kg6, 51...Rg4+ Kf5 52...Rxg8 Kxe6. This game reply differs from the possible king recapture, which is covered as analysis.

reviews.reason: A tempting pawn capture loses the attacker to a bishop. The checking rook move instead exposes a distant knight and wins it before the knight can countercheck.
reviews.distinctness: The learner must bypass the defended b6 pawn and stop one rank short to check with the same rook. The knight on h5 is far from all the king retreats, so the payoff needs no supporting guard.
reviews.solutionVi: Rb5+ — Xe đen từ b1 đến b5, chiếu Vua trắng trên hàng 5. Khi Vua trắng rời hàng này, Xe đen bắt Mã trắng ở h5. Nếu bắt Tốt b6 ngay, Tượng trắng có thể bắt lại Xe.
hintsVi: Vua trắng và Mã trắng cùng đứng trên hàng 5.
Xe đen có thể chiếu trên hàng 5 mà không cần bắt Tốt b6.
Đưa Xe đen từ b1 đến b5.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rb5+ aligns the checking rook with Kd5 and Nh5. White cannot use its knight’s counterchecks before responding to this direct check.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 20 roots were checked. Rxb6 Bxb6 loses the rook, and Rd1+ Ke5 does not expose the knight. The better quiet engine alternatives do not win material promptly and allow a knight check or escape, including Na5 Nf6+.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ke4, Kd4 and Kc4 are all the legal replies. Rxh5 is legal in each branch and the 36 immediate replies after those captures preserve the full knight gain.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces. Black is nominally ahead a rook for a bishop, but White still has bishop, knight and a far-advanced passed pawn. The skewer adds a full knight and is the single clear decision rather than routine conversion.
reviewNotes.provenance: Shapiro–Kurpiewski, 2 December 2025, TWIC 1622. The complete 178-ply game gives the exact board after 57.Nh5 and the played sequence 57...Rb5+ 58.Ke4 Rxh5. Archive checksum and White’s FM title are recorded.

reviews.reason: The checking skewer is the immediate answer to a promotion. It recovers from a material deficit even if the newly promoted queen trades for the rook.
reviews.distinctness: The source just promoted on e1, so the new queen is the target. The visible e-file check matters more than the tempting check along the third rank. The pawn race can be discussed separately.
reviews.solutionVi: Re8+ — Xe trắng từ b8 đến e8, chiếu Vua đen trên cột e. Khi Vua rời cột, Xe trắng bắt Hậu vừa phong cấp ở e1. Nếu Vua đen bắt lại Xe, Trắng vẫn có lợi vì đã đổi Xe lấy Hậu.
hintsVi: Hậu đen vừa xuất hiện ở ô nào? Hãy so sánh cột của Hậu và Vua đen.
Tìm nước chiếu đưa Xe trắng lên cùng cột với hai quân đen.
Đưa Xe trắng từ b8 đến e8.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The pawn’s promotion on e1 leaves Ke3 directly in front of the new queen. The e-file check is necessary to reach the queen before it moves.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 24 roots were compared. Rb3+ allows Kd4 and leaves the queen safe. Pawn pushes or a quiet move give Black time to use the queen.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All six king replies allow Rxe1. After Kf2 or Kd2, Kxe1 recaptures the rook and still leaves a queen-for-rook gain. All 24 immediate replies retain at least +400 cp in material. The checking move offers no material.
reviewNotes.level: Six pieces. The one move isolates the response to promotion. Pawn promotion later in the game is outside the exercise.
reviewNotes.provenance: The 155-ply TWIC 1664 game records e1=Q, 68.Re8+ Kf2 69.Rxe1 Kxe1. Full original replay and previous promotion frame are attached.

reviews.reason: A pawn makes the decisive close-range queen check safe. The apparent free knight capture fails to the king, and the skewer still gains material when White later takes the supporting pawn.
reviews.distinctness: The supporting pawn guards the attacking square e2, rather than guarding the rear capture square. That makes the difference between a safe contact check and the tempting Qxe3+ Kxe3.
reviews.solutionVi: Qe2+ — Hậu đen từ d2 đến e2, chiếu Vua trắng trên đường chéo e2–h5. Tốt đen ở d3 bảo vệ e2 nên Vua trắng không thể bắt Hậu. Khi Vua trắng rời đường chéo, Hậu đen bắt Tượng trắng ở h5. Nếu Vua trắng sau đó bắt Tốt d3, Đen vẫn giành lợi thế vật chất.
hintsVi: Vua trắng ở f3 và Tượng trắng ở h5 cùng đứng trên một đường chéo.
Tìm ô chiếu được Tốt đen ở d3 bảo vệ.
Đưa Hậu đen từ d2 đến e2.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The protected queen lands on e2 to check Kf3 along e2–h5 and expose Bh5. Without the pawn guarding e2, the nearby king could take the attacker.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 22 roots were checked. Qxe3+ Kxe3 and Qf2+ Kxf2 lose the queen, while Qg2+ also permits Nxg2. Quiet queen and king moves allow the bishop to leave or White to countercheck before the same short gain can be secured.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ke4 and Kg3 are the two legal replies. Qxh5 gains at least a bishop for a pawn through all 27 immediate replies. Nd5+ and Nc4+ do not attack the queen and neither causes immediate material recovery.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces, direct diagonal skewer and an obvious supporting pawn. Black is only 150 cp ahead in nominal material and still faces active minor pieces and White’s pawns. The net gain remains visible if White takes d3.
reviewNotes.provenance: Manukian–Javakhadze, 14 April 2026, TWIC 1641. Exact board after 49.Kf3 in the complete 132-ply game, then 49...Qe2+ 50.Ke4 Qxh5 was played. Archive checksum and Black’s IM title are retained.

reviews.reason: In an equal position White must select the right check. Black can take the already undefended g5 pawn, but this is the only king exit and it exposes the rook on d7.
reviews.distinctness: The bishop check closes the diagonal while White’s rook, king and pawn restrict the king’s escapes. Compare two natural checks that lose material. The single legal retreat captures a pawn, unlike the earlier bishop skewers that rely on an unoccupied retreat or a defender recapturing after the rear-piece capture.
reviews.solutionVi: Bh3+ — Tượng trắng từ f1 đến h3, chiếu Vua đen trên đường chéo h3–d7. Vua đen chỉ có thể bắt Tốt ở g5. Tượng trắng sau đó bắt Xe ở d7, nên Trắng bắt được Xe và chỉ mất một Tốt.
hintsVi: Tìm đường chéo đi qua Vua đen ở f5 và Xe đen ở d7.
Nếu chiếu từ d3, Xe đen có thể bắt Tượng. Hãy tìm ô chiếu trên đường chéo còn lại.
Đưa Tượng trắng từ f1 đến h3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The bishop on h3 checks Kf5 with Rd7 directly behind it. Re1 covers the e-file exits and Kg3 covers f4 and g4. The check moves the king off the only line to Rd7.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 20 legal roots are resolved and the engine comparison keeps the strongest quiet alternative, Re8, near equal. Bd3+ allows Rxd3+ and Re5+ allows Kxe5. Neither alternate check, nor any other root, produces a durable material gain within the teaching horizon. No rival mate was found.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kxg5 is the only legal reply to Bh3+. The g5 pawn is undefended already and the quiet move does not offer the moving bishop. After Bxd7, all 16 legal immediate replies retain a rook-for-pawn gain. The forced king capture is an immediate favourable exchange, without a separate pawn offer or preparation.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces, equal starting material, one quiet bishop check and a clearly visible rook behind the king. The playable line stops at Bh3+.
reviewNotes.provenance: Nguyen, Dinh Trung – Cardozo, C, Titled Tue 20 January 2026, TWIC 1629. Replayed 167 plies from the checksummed source. The original board follows 46...Kf5 and the actual game continued 47.Bh3+ Kxg5 48.Bxd7.

reviews.reason: The forcing diagonal check breaks an equal-material queen ending. Even if the white king takes the advanced black pawn, Black has gained the queen.
reviews.distinctness: Unlike the existing Qh3+ example, the credible quiet alternative is advancing Black’s own passed pawn rather than capturing an enemy pawn with check. The skewer must be played first even though the actual game then lets White take that pawn.
reviews.solutionVi: Qb3+ — Hậu đen từ c3 đến b3, chiếu Vua trắng trên đường chéo b3–f7. Khi Vua trắng rời đường chéo, Đen bắt Hậu ở f7. Nếu Vua trắng bắt Tốt b4 sau đó, Đen vẫn có lợi vì bắt được Hậu và chỉ mất một Tốt.
hintsVi: Vua d5 và Hậu f7 của Trắng cùng đứng trên đường chéo nào?
Đừng vội đẩy Tốt b4. Tìm nước chiếu nhắm tới Hậu trắng phía sau Vua.
Đưa Hậu đen từ c3 đến b3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Only Qb3+ checks through the king on d5 toward the queen on f7. It keeps the queen safe and forces the alignment to open at once.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Compared all 29 legal starts through two solver turns and their replies. After b3, Qg8 keeps the white queen safe. Qd3+ permits Ke5 without losing the queen. The tempting closer checks Qe5+ and Qc6+ allow immediate king captures. No other root secures short material or mate.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All five legal replies Kd6, Kc6, Ke5, Kc5 and Kd4 allow Qxf7. All 23 immediate recovery replies retain material. Kc5 Qxf7 Kxb4 is the strongest immediate recovery, reducing the gain from a queen to a queen for a pawn. Neither the check nor the capture offers the attacking queen.

reviews.reason: The long bishop check recovers the material deficit even against a king recapture. The other bishop check leaves the bishop en prise.

reviews.solutionVi: Bc4+ — Tượng trắng từ b5 đến c4, chiếu Vua đen trên đường chéo c4–g8. Khi Vua rời đường chéo, Tượng bắt Xe ở g8. Trong ván đấu, Vua đen lui về f8 rồi bắt lại Tượng ở g8. Đổi Tượng lấy Xe giúp Trắng cân bằng vật chất.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: From c4 the bishop checks the king on f7 with the rook directly behind on g8. The king must vacate the diagonal, exposing the rook to that same bishop. White cannot take the rook directly from the starting position.

reviewNotes.provenance: The complete 154-ply TWIC 1634 game replays to the exact frame after 51.Ke5. The original line 51...Re6+ 52.Kd4 Rxe2 demonstrates the same payoff.

reviews.reason: The correct adjacent bishop check is safe because the h4 pawn guards it. The other adjacent check loses the bishop to the king. The skewer earns a full rook from a material deficit.
reviews.distinctness: White chooses between checks by the same bishop. Here the correct checking square is adjacent to the king and needs a pawn guard. This contrasts with the earlier Black bishop exercise where the distant check is safe and the closer check loses the bishop.
reviews.solutionVi: Bg5+ — Tượng trắng từ h6 đến g5, chiếu Vua đen trên đường chéo g5–d8. Tốt trắng ở h4 bảo vệ ô g5, nên Vua đen không thể bắt Tượng. Khi Vua rời đường chéo, Tượng trắng bắt Xe ở d8. Nếu chiếu từ g7, Vua đen có thể bắt Tượng.

reviews.reason: The queen must check from the side of the king opposite the rook. Checking from the rook’s side gives up the queen, while the safe rank check wins the rook.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: From g2 the bishop checks Kf3 along g2–d5, with Rd5 behind it. White’s king on g1 protects g2 from a king capture. Moving the black king exposes the rook without requiring another preparatory move.

Here the solver is behind and must seize the single opportunity before the bishop can escape or take a pawn.
